findings.test_name: addFiles — silent rejection of unsupported file types
findings.description: When the user picks a file whose extension is NOT in SUPPORTED_EXT (['.pdf', '.csv', '.txt']) — e.g. a .docx, .xlsx, .png — the addFiles() function silently skips it (the continue statement on line 328 of UnifiedImportModal.tsx). The file is never added to row.files. The Preview button stays disabled showing 'Preview (0 rows)'. No error message, no visual feedback, no toast, no alert appears. The user sees nothing happen and believes the upload failed.
findings.code_snippet: if (!SUPPORTED_EXT.some((e) => name.endsWith(e))) continue  // silent drop — no user feedback
findings.expected: When a file is rejected (wrong extension or oversized), the UI should display an inline error message in the row or beneath the dropzone (e.g. 'Only PDF, CSV, and TXT files are supported. The following files were skipped: statement.docx') and keep the dropzone interactive.
findings.observed: File is silently discarded. previewBtnDisabled=true, previewBtnText='Preview (0 rows)', no role=alert element in DOM, dropzone text unchanged, attachedFileCount=0.
reproduction_steps: Open UnifiedImportModal via '+ Import accounts' header button
Select any account in the row 1 dropdown
Click the dashed dropzone to open the file picker
In the OS dialog, switch to 'All Files' and select any .docx or .xlsx or .png file
Observe: no file appears in the row, Preview button stays disabled, no error shown
findings.root_cause: The addFiles() filter (UnifiedImportModal.tsx:319-334) iterates incoming files and silently continues past any file that fails extension or size checks. There is no branch to accumulate rejected filenames and surface them to the user.
findings.also_affects: The MAX_FILE_MB (10 MB) size check on line 329 has the same silent-rejection behavior.
findings.note_on_input_element: The hidden file input has accept='.pdf,.csv,.txt' which hints the OS picker to filter by type, but users can bypass this by selecting 'All Files' in the OS dialog. The in-code filter is therefore the correct enforcement layer — but it must tell the user what was rejected.

findings.test_name: Hidden input display:none — cross-browser file picker activation
findings.reproducible: Chromium: not reproduced (works). Safari: likely to reproduce (not tested in this session).
findings.description: The file <input> uses the shadcn/ui Input component (which wraps @base-ui/react/input) with className='hidden'. The Tailwind 'hidden' class computes to display:none on the rendered <input> element (confirmed: getComputedStyle returned display='none', boundingRect={w:0,h:0}). The dropzone div's onClick calls fileRef.current?.click(). In Chromium, calling .click() on a display:none file input within a user-gesture callback works and opens the OS file picker. In Safari 16 and earlier, browser security restrictions may block programmatic .click() on a hidden file input even within a user-gesture handler. The correct pattern is to use a <label htmlFor=inputId> or position the input with opacity:0 / position:absolute / width:0 / height:0 rather than display:none.
findings.expected: File input should be reachable in all major browsers. Pattern: position:absolute; opacity:0; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden (or a <label> wrapping the input) instead of display:none.
findings.observed: Input has display:none (from Tailwind 'hidden' class). In Chromium (tested): click propagates correctly and file picker opens. In Safari: NOT tested in this session — flag as warning requiring Safari manual verification.
findings.ref_check: fileRef.current correctly points to the INPUT element (confirmed via React fiber inspection: hook index 5 has current='INPUT'). The ref attachment itself is working.
findings.click_mechanism_check: Confirmed: dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click')) on the dropzone div triggers the file input click and opens the file chooser dialog in Chromium.
